steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evaluation means making informed judgements about how effectively a dance communicates its intention

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Effective evaluation requires clear criteria — such as how well movement, structure and design serve the intention

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evaluation builds on description and analysis — you must first understand what happens and how it works

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A judgement must always be supported with specific evidence from the dance

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between analysis and evaluation? | Q: Why must evaluation be supported by evidence? | Q: Give two criteria you could use to evaluate a dance work.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Analysis explains how and why choreographic choices work; evaluation judges how effective they are — analysis is about understanding, evaluation is about judging success. | Evidence grounds your judgement in fact; without it, evaluation is mere opinion and gains no marks in the AQA exam. | Clarity of intention (how clearly the purpose is communicated) and cohesion (how well the elements work together as a unified whole).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always start evaluation by stating the choreographic intention — then judge how well it is achieved Use phrases like 'highly effective because…' or 'less successful as…' to show clear evaluative judgement Support every judgement with at least one specific example from the dance In self-evaluation, balance strengths and weaknesses — examiners value reflective honesty Remember: evaluation is the highest-level skill — it demonstrates mature, independent critical thinking
